title: Judaism in Yemen and the History of the Kiswah
overview: This episode explores the historical introduction of Judaism and Christianity into the Arabian Peninsula, focusing on the conversion of the Yemeni king Tibban As'ad. It details the prophecy of the Prophet's ﷺ migration to Madinah and the origin of the Kiswah covering the Ka'bah.
lessons: Generosity and high character, even toward enemies, can be a powerful form of dawah.
Sincerity in seeking the truth can lead a person from the darkness of shirk to the light of tawhid.
Allah protects His sacred places, and those who intend harm to the Ka'bah or the city of the Prophet ﷺ face divine consequences.
The importance of relying on scholars and people of knowledge to avoid being misled by the treacherous.

chapters.title: Introduction and Religious Context
chapters.summary: The lecture begins by reviewing the historical landscape of the Arabian Peninsula before the birth of the Prophet ﷺ. While Makkah was dominated by idol worship introduced by Amr ibn Luhayy, other regions like Madinah, Khaybar, and Najran were home to significant Jewish and Christian populations. Understanding these religious dynamics is essential for comprehending the Prophet's ﷺ later interactions with these groups. The speaker aims to trace the roots of how these faiths arrived in the region.
key_points: The Arabian Peninsula was home to idol worshippers, Jews, and Christians.
A delegation of Christians from Najran visited the Prophet ﷺ in Madinah.
The Jews of Madinah and Khaybar originally migrated from the region of Sham.
Amr ibn Luhayy is identified as the person who brought idolatry back to the peninsula.

chapters.title: Rabiah ibn Nasr and the Dream of Conquest
chapters.summary: The history of monotheistic religions in Yemen is linked to King Rabiah ibn Nasr. During a time when Yemen was steeped in idolatry and soothsaying, the King had a troubling dream that was interpreted as a future conquest by the Ethiopians. Fearing for his dynasty, he sent his family to Hirah in Iraq. This chapter also explains the royal titles used in the ancient world, such as Tubba for Yemen, Qaysar for Rome, and Kisra for Persia.
key_points: Rabiah ibn Nasr was a king of Yemen whose dream predicted an Ethiopian takeover.
The interpretation suggested the conquest would happen in 60 to 70 years.
Tubba (تبع) was the honorary title for the rulers of Yemen.
The title for the ruler of Ethiopia was Najashi (نجاشي).

chapters.title: The Siege of Yathrib and a King's Change of Heart
chapters.summary: One of the successors of Rabiah, Tibban As'ad, embarked on a business trip to Syria and left his son in Yathrib. After his son was murdered by the locals, Tibban returned with an army to destroy the city. However, he became fascinated by the character of the people of Yathrib, who fought his army by day but provided them with food and provisions by night. This display of extraordinary generosity even toward an enemy began to soften the King's heart.
key_points: Tibban As'ad was a powerful and business-savvy Tubba of Yemen.
His son was killed by the people of Yathrib during a business expedition.
The people of Yathrib fought during the day but sent food to the Yemeni army at night.
This hospitality even during warfare was a unique trait of the Yathribi people.

chapters.title: The Prophecy of the Promised Land
chapters.summary: While besieging Yathrib, Tibban As'ad was approached by two Jewish scholars who warned him that he could never destroy the city. They explained that Yathrib was divinely protected because it was the destined place of migration for a future Prophet, as mentioned in the Tawrah. Impressed by this revelation and the teachings of monotheism, Tibban As'ad abandoned his siege and accepted Judaism. This marked the beginning of Judaism's official presence in the Yemeni royal court.
key_points: Jewish scholars from Yathrib informed the King that the city was destined for a future Prophet.
Knowledge of the Prophet's ﷺ migration was found in the Tawrah (توراة).
Tibban As'ad converted to Judaism after studying with the scholars.
The King abandoned his plans to destroy Yathrib out of respect for the prophecy.

chapters.title: The Treachery of Hudhayl and Respect for the Ka'bah
chapters.summary: As Tibban As'ad traveled through the Hijaz, the tribe of Hudhayl attempted to trick him into attacking Makkah by promising him buried treasures around the Ka'bah. Their true motive was to see the King destroyed by divine wrath for violating the sanctuary. Once again, the Jewish scholars advised the King of the Ka'bah's sanctity as the House of Allah. Following their advice, the King performed Tawaf and showed great reverence for the site rather than pillaging it.
key_points: The tribe of Hudhayl tried to pit the Yemenis against the Makkans.
The Ka'bah was known by scholars as the House of Allah on earth.
Hudhayl falsely promised gold and treasures to lure Tibban into a trap.
Tibban As'ad followed the scholars' advice and performed Tawaf around the Ka'bah.

chapters.title: The First Kiswah and the Trial by Fire
chapters.summary: While in Makkah, Tibban As'ad had a dream that he was covering the Ka'bah, leading him to become the first person in history to provide the Kiswah using luxurious Yemeni cloth. This tradition continued through the generations until the time of Abdul Muttalib. Upon returning to Yemen, the King challenged his people to accept Judaism. The matter was decided by a 'trial by fire,' where a sacred fire consumed the idolatrous soothsayers but left the Jewish scholars unharmed, resulting in the mass conversion of the Yemeni people.
key_points: Tibban As'ad was the first to put a cloth cover (Kiswah) on the Ka'bah.
The tradition of replacing the Kiswah annually was established by Abdul Muttalib.
A 'trial by fire' was used in Yemen to determine religious truth.
The episode concludes with a mention of Abrahah the Ethiopian and the Year of the Elephant.

segments.translit: Bismillāhi r-Raḥmāni r-Raḥīm. Al-ḥamdu lillāhi Rabbi l-ʿālamīn, wa-ṣallallāhu wa-sallama wa-bāraka ʿalā nabiyyinā Muḥammadin wa-ʿalā ālihi wa-ṣaḥbihi ajmaʿīn. Rabbi shraḥ lī ṣadrī wa-yassir lī amrī wa-ḥlul ʿuqdatan min lisānī yafqahū qawlī. Allāhumma ʿallimnā mā yanfaʿunā wa-nfaʿnā bimā ʿallamtanā wa-zidnā ʿilmā.

segments.text: Last week when we started this class on the [[Seerah|سيرة]] of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, I mentioned that it's important before we actually start with the birth of the Prophet ﷺ and his messengership, we need to go back a little bit in history and talk about the civilization in the Arabian Peninsula at that time, what type of a society was it that the Prophet ﷺ came into.

And last week we talked about the beginnings of Makkan civilization with [[Ibrahim|إبراهيم]] ('alayhis-salam) and how he left his wife and his son in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], and how the civilization started from then, and how it was a civilization of [[tawhid|توحيد]], where Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] alone was worshipped in the Arabian Peninsula.

And then we spoke about how [[Amr ibn Luhayy|عمرو بن لحي]] brought [[shirk|شرك]] back into the Arabian Peninsula, how he brought the worship of idols into the Arabian Peninsula, and that lasted until the time of the Prophet ﷺ, that the people of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] were worshippers of idols.

And the Prophet ﷺ said about this man that we spoke about last week, [[Amr ibn Luhayy|عمرو بن لحي]], the man who brought idolatry back into the Arabian Peninsula, [[Amr ibn Luhayy|عمرو بن لحي]], the Prophet ﷺ said about him:

segments.translit: Ra'aytu ʿAmra bna Luḥayyin yajurru amʿā'ahu fī n-nār.

segments.text: I saw [[Amr ibn Luhayy|عمرو بن لحي]] dragging his intestines in the Fire. So this is the punishment of this man who brought [[shirk|شرك]] into the Arabian Peninsula.

But if you look at the Qur'an, you see that Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] addresses a number of different types of people who were present at that time. He addresses the [[mushrikin|مشركين]], who were the people of [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]]. But if you look in some other [[ayat|آيَات]] of the Qur'an, you see how Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] also addresses the Jews and the Christians.

So that means during the time of the Prophet ﷺ in the Arabian Peninsula, there were also Jews, and there were also Christians. And we know from the history of the Prophet ﷺ in [[Madinah|مدينة]] that there were Jews in [[Madinah|مدينة]], and there were many incidents and incidents that happened between the Prophet ﷺ and the Jews of [[Madinah|مدينة]]. And we also know that the Prophet ﷺ had interactions with Christians as well. A delegation of Christians from [[Najran|نجران]], they came to [[Madinah|مدينة]], and they met the Prophet ﷺ, and they had a discussion with him.

So there were idol worshippers in the Arabian Peninsula, and we spoke about how they came to be in the Arabian Peninsula by the works, the evil of [[Amr ibn Luhayy|عمرو بن لحي]], who brought idol worshipping back into the Arabian Peninsula. Today we want to talk a little bit about how Christianity and Judaism came into the Arabian Peninsula, because we need to understand these things so we can understand the Prophet ﷺ's interactions with all of these groups of people, how he interacted with the [[kuffar|كفار]], the [[mushrikin|مشركين]], the idol worshippers of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], how he interacted with the Christians, how he interacted with the Jews. So we need to know a little bit about the history of all of these people and how they came to be in the Arabian Peninsula in the first place.

And we know that during the time of the Prophet ﷺ, who were the rulers of [[Yemen|اليمن]]? The rulers of [[Yemen|اليمن]] were not Arabs. They were Persians. So during the time of the Prophet ﷺ, the Persians were ruling [[Yemen|اليمن]]. And at that time, [[Yemen|اليمن]], it had Christians and Jews in [[Yemen|اليمن]] as well. And [[Najran|نجران]], as we mentioned, [[Najran|نجران]] is a city that is on the border of [[Yemen|اليمن]]. It is in present-day Saudi Arabia, in the south part of present-day Saudi Arabia. [[Najran|نجران]] was a city that was completely Christian. So how did this come about?

As for [[Madinah|مدينة]], and it was only named [[Madinah|مدينة]], [[al-Madinah al-Nabawiyyah|الْمَدِينَة النَّبَوِيَّة]], the [[Madinah|مدينة]], the city of the Prophet ﷺ, it was only called [[Madinah|مدينة]] after the Prophet ﷺ came there and migrated there. Before it was called [[Madinah|مدينة]], what was the name of this city? Does anybody know the name of this city? [[Yathrib|يثرب]], correct. The name of this city was [[Yathrib|يثرب]]. And there were Jews in [[Yathrib|يثرب]] as well, also in [[Khaybar|خيبر]], which is a city about 150 kilometers north of [[Madinah|مدينة]], there were Jews there as well. And the way that the Jews came to [[Yathrib|يثرب]] and to [[Khaybar|خيبر]], they came from [[Sham|شام]]. They came from the Greater Syria area. There were Jews up there, and they migrated southwards. They came to [[Madinah|مدينة]], and they came to [[Khaybar|خيبر]], and they settled over there. So this is how the Jews came into these cities.

Now, what was the origin of how these religions came into [[Yemen|اليمن]] and how they came into the Arabian Peninsula? As we mentioned, [[Yemen|اليمن]] is the root country of the Arabs. The original Arabs, they came from [[Yemen|اليمن]]. And only after the water supply of [[Yemen|اليمن]] was depleted, that's when they started moving around in the Arabian Peninsula to different parts and inhabiting different parts of that land. So most of the historians, they start speaking about the history of how Judaism and Christianity entered into the Arabian Peninsula by starting with the history of one of the rulers of [[Yemen|اليمن]], and his name was [[Rabiah ibn Nasr|ربيعة بن نصر]]. He was a ruler of [[Yemen|اليمن]], and his name was [[Rabiah ibn Nasr|ربيعة بن نصر]].

And as we know, after [[Amr ibn Luhayy|عمرو بن لحي]], idol worshipping became very common throughout the Arabian Peninsula, and that actually penetrated [[Yemen|اليمن]] as well. So the people of [[Yemen|اليمن]], they were idol worshippers. They used to commit [[shirk|شرك]]. They used to consult magicians and soothsayers and fortune tellers and this type of a thing. So [[Rabiah ibn Nasr|ربيعة بن نصر]], he was the king of [[Yemen|اليمن]] at that time.

And he had a dream. He had a dream, and he went to some of the soothsayers and fortune tellers for the interpretation of that dream. And he was told that the interpretation of that dream is that in some point in the future that the [[Abhash|أحباش]], the Habashis—and these are the people who inhabit current day what is called Ethiopia—the [[Abhash|أحباش]] will rule [[Yemen|اليمن]]. Now [[Rabiah ibn Nasr|ربيعة بن نصر]], he's the king of [[Yemen|اليمن]], and he is being told that the interpretation of his dream is that the [[Abhash|أحباش]], the Ethiopians are going to come and take over [[Yemen|اليمن]].

So he became worried about this. He became scared about this, and he feared for his family. And when he asked them when is this going to happen, around when do you think this is going to happen, they told him maybe 60 to 70 years. Maybe in 60 to 70 years, the rulers of [[Yemen|اليمن]] are going to be Habashis.

And he became scared about this for his family, because he thought, okay, when they come and they take over, you know, there's probably going to be a lot of bloodshed, a lot of killing and this type of thing. So I need to keep my family safe. So what he did is he sent his family to a place called [[Hirah|حيرة]] in modern day Iraq. He sent his family to Iraq, but he stayed in [[Yemen|اليمن]] because he was the king; he had to stay in [[Yemen|اليمن]]. And he kept one of his sons with him as well, because his intention was that when he died, then his son is going to take over the kingdom as well.

And when his son became the ruler of [[Yemen|اليمن]], he kept a son with him as well to take over after he died, and this continued for some time. And the ruler of [[Yemen|اليمن]], the title for the ruler of [[Yemen|اليمن]] was called the [[Tubba|تبع]]. [[Tubba|تبع]]. Just like the title for any of the rulers of Rome, they were called [[Qaysar|قيصر]], the title of any of the rulers of Persia, they were called [[Kisra|كسرى]], the title of the rulers of Ethiopia, they were called [[Najashi|نجاشي]]. Right, this was a title, an honorary title for the rulers of these lands, just like in the past, the rulers of Egypt, what were they known as? They were known as [[Firaun|فرعون]]. Yes, the rulers of Egypt were [[Firaun|فرعون]].

So the ruler of [[Yemen|اليمن]], he was known as [[Tubba|تبع]]. And this continued for some time. The sons of [[Rabiah ibn Nasr|ربيعة بن نصر]], the sons and the grandsons, they kept this kingdom alive, and they were continuing in their roles as the leaders of [[Yemen|اليمن]] until a time came where one of the sons, one of the grandsons of [[Rabiah ibn Nasr|ربيعة بن نصر]], his name was [[Tibban As'ad|تبان أسعد]]. [[Tibban As'ad|تبان أسعد]], he was the [[Tubba|تبع]], he was the ruler of [[Yemen|اليمن]]. And he was a very generous man. He was a very powerful man. He was a very rich man. And he was very business-oriented as well. He was business savvy. He was the king of [[Yemen|اليمن]], but he also continued to do his business and his trade. So one day, he was going on a business expedition from [[Yemen|اليمن]] to [[Sham|شام]], all the way from the south of the Arabian Peninsula, [[Yemen|اليمن]], he was going all the way north up to [[Sham|شام]], Greater Syria. So he was going there for some business prospect, and he took...
[[Tibban As'ad|تبان أسعد]] took his son with him on that journey.
On the way from [[Yemen|اليمن]] to Syria, they passed through [[Yathrib|يثرب]].
They passed through [[Yathrib|يثرب]], which later on came to be known as [[Madinah|مدينة]], but at that time it was [[Yathrib|يثرب]].
And he saw an opportunity there in [[Yathrib|يثرب]] to do some business as well.
But he had to go to Syria, he had to go to [[Sham|شام]] to do his business.
So what he decided to do is he left his son in [[Yathrib|يثرب]].
He said, "Okay, you stay here in [[Yathrib|يثرب]], you take care of the business, I'm going to go up to [[Sham|شام]] and take care of the business there."
So he went to [[Sham|شام]] and he left his son in [[Yathrib|يثرب]].
Now, his son in [[Yathrib|يثرب]] and the people of the city, the people of [[Yathrib|يثرب]], they had some fights and some arguments.
And eventually, the son of [[Tibban As'ad|تبان أسعد]], he was killed by the people of [[Yathrib|يثرب]].
He was murdered, he was killed by the people of [[Yathrib|يثرب]].
Now, when his father heard about this, when the news reached him, he left [[Sham|شام]] and he came back to [[Yathrib|يثرب]].
And he ordered an army to come from [[Yemen|اليمن]] as well, to come to [[Yathrib|يثرب]] and to fight the people of [[Yathrib|يثرب]], to take revenge for his son.
So he decided to take revenge for his son and he wanted to kill the people of [[Yathrib|يثرب]] and he wanted to destroy the city.
So he called the army from [[Yemen|اليمن]] and they were fighting with the people of [[Yathrib|يثرب]] and the war began.
And this war, it lasted for some time.

And this war, it lasted for some time. And while this war was going on, the [[Tubba|تبع]] whose name was [[Tibban As'ad|تبان أسعد]], as we mentioned, he was amazed at some of the characteristics of the people of [[Madinah|مدينة]] even at that time.
Even at that time he was amazed by some of the characteristics and the personality traits of the people of [[Yathrib|يثرب]].
What did they use to do? What was he amazed with?
They used to fight in the daytime. They used to fight in the day, but then when nightfall came, both sides would retreat to their camps.
And then they would continue fighting when the sun came up again, because you can't fight in the dark.
It's not like how it is today where you have all sorts of lights and electricity and this type of thing. No, when it's dark, it's dark.
So they didn't used to fight in the night. Both sides had an agreement, of course, that when nightfall comes, both camps or both parties have to retreat to their camps.
So they would fight during the day and when the sun set, they would both retreat to their camps.
Now, [[Tibban As'ad|تبان أسعد]] and his army, they were in their camp.
And during the nights, the people of [[Yathrib|يثرب]], they would send them food and drink and they would send them all sorts of provisions.
And in the daytime they would be fighting with them, but in the night, they would show their generosity by sending them food and drink and whatever they needed.
So [[Tibban As'ad|تبان أسعد]], he was amazed at this.
He was like, "Who honors their enemies in such a way? We are fighting these people, we are killing these people and they are killing us."
"But at the same time, when we're not fighting, during the night they're sending us food and drink and they're honoring us and they're showing us such generosity."
He was absolutely amazed at this. He was like, "This is something that is unbelievable. I've never seen anything like this before."
And if you think about it, it really is amazing. It really is something that is amazing.
But still, out of his anger at these people for the fact that they killed his son, he still wanted to continue to fight them, and he continued to fight them.

Now, as we mentioned, [[Yathrib|يثرب]], it had some Jews there because some of the Jews from [[Sham|شام]], from greater Syria, they had migrated to [[Yathrib|يثرب]]. So there were some Jews there too.

So two of the scholars of these Jews, while this fighting was going on, two of the scholars of the Jews who were settled in [[Yathrib|يثرب]], who had migrated from [[Sham|شام]], they went to [[Tibban As'ad|تبان أسعد]].
And they said, "We need to sit down and we need to talk to you about what's going on."
So he said, "Okay, let's talk. Let's have a discussion."
These two scholars of the Jews, they asked [[Tibban|تبان]], they asked the [[Tubba|تبع]], "What do you want? What is your goal in this fighting? What do you want to do? What is your objective?"
And the [[Tubba|تبع]] said, "I want to kill these people, I want to destroy this city."
"They killed my son, I will not rest until the city of [[Yathrib|يثرب]] is in ruins. It has to be destroyed completely. I will take revenge for my son."
Now, these two scholars of the Jews, they said to him, "[[Wallahi|والله]], you will never be able to do it to this city."

"[[Wallahi|والله]], you will never be able to destroy this city, no matter how many people you bring, no matter how many weapons you bring, no matter what type of destruction you think you can wreak here, you will never be able to destroy this city."
"Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] will destroy you before you are able to destroy this city, this city in particular."
And then he was amazed at this speech. He said, "Why do you say this? What is special about this place?"
And they said to him, "This is a place, this is a city where a Prophet is going to come and migrate to this city."

"A Prophet that's going to come in the future, he's going to come and he's going to settle in this city. So there's no way that Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] is going to allow you to destroy this city."
And then he said to him, "What are you talking about? What Prophet is going to come and come to this city? How do you know this? Where are you getting this information?"
Then they said, "We get this information from our book, the [[Tawrah|توراة]]."
And this was the book that Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] revealed to [[Musa|موسى]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]]. And it had a lot of information about the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.
It really did. It had information about the Prophet ﷺ in the [[Tawrah|توراة]].
And the true Jews, the people who really believed in the [[Tawrah|توراة]], they knew that a Prophet was going to come.

So they told the [[Tubba|تبع]], they said, "This is the city a Prophet is going to come and migrate to the city, and we get the information that we are telling you from our book, the [[Tawrah|توراة]]."
So he became amazed at this. He had never heard about this type of thing before.
So he got interested in it and he asked them, "What is this book, the [[Tawrah|توراة]]? What does it teach you?"
And he started to study it with them and they started to teach him about [[tawhid|توحيد]], the oneness of Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]].
And they taught him the message of [[Musa|موسى]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]]. They taught him the [[Tawrah|توراة]] and he was very impressed with it.
He was very impressed with it and at the end of the conversation and these teachings, he became a Jew.
[[Tibban As'ad|تبان أسعد]], he accepted Judaism and he became a Jew.
And he left the fighting in [[Madinah|مدينة]]. He abandoned it.
Then he left the city and he was on his way, and he was in the [[Hijaz|حجاز]].
The [[Hijaz|حجاز]] is the area of present day Saudi Arabia where [[Madinah|مدينة]] is included in that, [[Makkah|مكة]] is included in that, it's a general region that is in the Arabian Peninsula.
So there was a tribe in the [[Hijaz|حجاز]] that occupied the [[Hijaz|حجاز]] and this tribe was called [[Hudhayl|هذيل]].
The tribe of [[Hudhayl|هذيل]], and they hated the people of [[Makkah|مكة]].
The tribe of [[Hudhayl|هذيل]], they hated the people of [[Makkah|مكة]] and they also hated the people of [[Yemen|اليمن]].
They hated the people of [[Makkah|مكة]] and they hated the people of [[Yemen|يمن]].
And when they saw that the [[Tubba|تبع]] is in town, the [[Tubba|تبع]] is around here, the leader of [[Yemen|يمن]] is here.
They saw this as an opportunity to eliminate both of their enemies, to eliminate the [[Yamanis|يمنيين]] and to eliminate the people of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] by pitting them against each other.
So what did the people of [[Hudhayl|هذيل]], what did they say to the [[Tubba|تبع]] when they met him?
They said, "Before you leave this place, do you want treasures and gold and jewels?"
And he said, "Of course. I mean, if it's available, you know, if there's treasures and gold and jewels that I can take, of course I want it."
So they said to him, "There is a place in [[Makkah|مكة]], there is a house in [[Makkah|مكة]] and in that house and around that house, there is jewels and gold and treasures buried there."
And what is this house that he's talking about? He's talking about the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]]. The [[Ka'bah|كعبة]].
And it's true that the Arabs, out of their respect and their honor for the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]], they used to actually bury gold and jewels and other treasure items around the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]].
So it was full of treasures all around buried there.
So these people of [[Hudhayl|هذيل]], they told the [[Tubba|تبع]], "There is this house..."
And remember, the [[Tubba|تبع]] is someone who just accepted Judaism. He doesn't really know anything about the religion. He doesn't know what the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] is or anything about it.
All he knows is what these people told him: there is this house in the city of [[Makkah|مكة]] and around it there is a lot of valuable stuff buried there.
So you can go ahead and and get it.
So he became, you know, he decided, "Yeah, I want to do that. I want to go and get it."
So he started preparing his army and getting them ready to go to [[Makkah|مكة]] and overtake the people of [[Makkah|مكة]] so they could extract these treasures from around the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]].
Now, these two scholars of the Jews, the people who originally gave him [[dawah|دعوة]] to become a Jew, they were around. He kept them around.
And when they saw him getting ready and they saw him getting his army ready, they asked him, "What are you doing? Who are you getting ready to fight? We see you preparing your army."

And then he told them. He said, "I was told by this tribe of [[Hudhayl|هذيل]] that there is a house in the city of [[Makkah|مكة]] and around that house there is buried a lot of valuable treasure items, gold, jewels, and other things."
"And I want to go there with my army and I want to extract this treasure."
So these two scholars of the Jews, they said, "[[Wallahi|والله]], these people of [[Hudhayl|هذيل]], they don't want good for you, they only want your destruction."
"They want you to be destroyed, because if you go and try to do anything to the house..."
Yes, that house that they're talking about, then Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] will destroy you. And then he said, 'Why? What is it?'
He said, 'That is the only house of Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] that we know on this earth at this time.'
That is the house of Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]]. You try to do anything to that house and the destruction of Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] will come to you.
So don't listen to these people, they're trying to trick you. They want you to be destroyed.
They want you to go ahead and destroy the people of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] and then they want Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] to destroy you for trying to violate the sanctity of His house.
So don't do it. So he was surprised. He said, 'Okay.' He was very, very attentive to these two scholars.

He listened to whatever they had to say. So he said, 'Okay, I'm not going to do it. So what should I do? Now we're around [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], we're already in the area. What should I do now that we're here?'

They said, 'You should respect the house of Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]]. Rather than trying to extract those treasures that are buried around there, you respect the house of Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]].'
Go to the house of Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] and make [[tawaf|طواف]]. Go to the house of Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] and make [[tawaf|طواف]].
And then he said, 'Okay.' But he noticed that when he went there to do [[tawaf|طواف]], those two scholars, they were not making [[tawaf|طواف]].

And then he asked, 'What about you? I'm going to do as you told me to do, respect the house of Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] and make [[tawaf|طواف]] around this house, but what about you? Why don't you do it?'
And they said to him, 'We are scholars, we are people of knowledge. And at this time, the people of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] have filled this house with idols.'
It is filled with idols, objects of worship besides Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]]. So it is not appropriate for us, you know, as people of knowledge, as people of scholars...
...to make [[tawaf|طواف]] around the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] while it's in this situation when idols are in it.
But as for the common people like you, you can do it. But for us, we can't do it at this time until it is cleansed from the idols.

So he understood that, he said, 'Okay.' And he went to [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] and he made [[tawaf|طواف]] of the house of Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] and he showed his respect to the house of Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]].

And he stayed in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] for the night and he slept. And when he slept, when the [[Tubba|تبّع]] of [[Yemen|اليمن]], [[Tabban As'ad|تبان أسعد]], when he slept in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], he had a dream.

He had a dream that he was covering the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] with a cloth. He was putting a cloth cover around the house of Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]], which is called the [[kiswah|كسوة]], the cover of the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]].

He had this dream. So when he had this dream, he ordered for a cloth to be sent from [[Yemen|اليمن]], from the very luxurious and beautiful cloth of [[Yemen|اليمن]], to come so that he can put this [[kiswah|كسوة]] around the house of Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]].
[[kiswah|كسوة الكعبة]]. Before that time, the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] was a bare structure, it didn't have any cover around it.
And [[Tibban As'ad|تبان أسعد]], the [[Tubba|تبع]] of [[Yemen|اليمن]], he was the first person in history to put a cover, to put a [[kiswah|كسوة]] around the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]].
And it continued every year. Every year they would put a new [[kiswah|كسوة]] on the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]].
But they would not remove the old one. They would put a new one over the old one.
Every year they would put a new covering over the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]], but they would not remove the old one.
Rather the new covering would just cover the old covering. And this went on for many years.

This went on for many years. Every year they're putting a [[kiswah|كسوة]] on the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]], and the next year it's doubled, and the next year another layer, the next year another layer, the next year another layer, and this kept going on and on and on for years.
And it lasted actually up to the time of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], up to the time of the grandfather of the Prophet [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]], [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]].

And at that time they noticed that there are so many layers of the [[kiswah|كسوة]] on this [[Ka'bah|كعبة]], so many layers of cloth covering it over the years, that they were afraid that the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] would collapse.

That the structure of the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] would not be able to support this heaviness. So they decided, the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]] in the time of [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]], they decided to remove all of those old covers...
...and put a new cover on it. And every subsequent year they would put a new cover, but they would remove the old cover.
So every year, remove the old cover and put a new cover, remove the old cover and put a new cover every year.
And that tradition continues up to our present time today. Every year they remove the old [[kiswah|كسوة]] of the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] and they put a new [[kiswah|كسوة]] of the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] over.

This has been going on for since the time of [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]], a new [[kiswah|كسوة]] every year. And if you go back to the time even before that of [[Tibban As'ad|تبان أسعد]], he is the one who actually started the concept of putting a cover around the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]].
We actually have a piece of that [[kiswah|كسوة]], the old, one of the old [[kiswah|كسوات]] in the library of this [[masjid|مسجد]].

If you go and you see, you know, you see on the bookshelf right when you enter the library on your left side, you will see a framed piece of one of the previous years' [[kiswah|كسوة]] of the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]].

So they continue this tradition every year putting a new covering over the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]]. So this is what the [[Tubba|تبّع]] of [[Yemen|اليمن]], [[Tabban As'ad|تبان أسعد]], did in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].
Then, after he was completed with this, he returned back to [[Yemen|اليمن]]. He went back to his country, he went back to [[Yemen|اليمن]].
And he brought these two scholars of the Jews with him to [[Yemen|اليمن]] as well. They were accompanying him now wherever he goes.
Because he wanted them to be with him. He had accepted Judaism, he had become a Jew.
And he wanted these two scholars with him to invite the people to Judaism as well. So he got them back with him to [[Yemen|اليمن]]...

...because he said, 'I want you guys to come to [[Yemen|اليمن]] and I want to invite my people to accept the [[Tawrah|توراة]] and to become Jews as well. So I need your help, you come with me.' So they came with him.
So when the [[Tubba|تبع]] came back to [[Yemen|اليمن]], he called on his people to accept Judaism.
And they said, "We will not take this type of a decision until we consult our fire."
They used to have a fire. You know, they used to worship many objects: stones and idols and this type of thing, and one of the things that they used to hold holy was a fire that they had.
And this fire, it was encased in a structure that had a door.
So there was a fire and it was covered around in a structure, and there was a door to this structure.
So whenever two people would have some kind of an argument or some type of a disagreement with each other, they would go to that fire to decide who is right and who is wrong.

So what they would do, the two people, they would go to the fire, and they would open the door, and whoever the fire came to first—you know how a fire is, you know, if you open a door to it, it will come out—

so they would go to the front of that fire, someone would stand on one side and another person would stand on the other side, and they would open the door to that structure, and the fire would come out.

They went back to [[Yemen|اليمن]]. And [[Yemen|اليمن]] was a place that was full of [[shirk|شرك]], and they used to consult soothsayers and fortune tellers and, you know, these type of evil liars about their affairs.
So when the [[Tubba|تبّع]] came back to [[Yemen|اليمن]], he called on his people to accept Judaism.

The [[Tubba|تبع]] came back to [[Yemen|اليمن]] to invite his people to Judaism. They said, "We will not make any decision in this affair until we go to the fire, and we will see if what you're telling us is correct or not."

So the [[Tubba|تبع]] looked at his two companions, the two scholars of the Jews. He looked at them like, "What do you think about this?" They said, "Okay, let them do it. Let them go ahead and do that."

So they gathered their fortune-tellers and soothsayers, and on the other side, these two scholars of the Jews. So the two scholars of the Jews were standing on one side of the door, and the fortune-tellers and the soothsayers were standing on the other side of the door.

And they opened the door, and the fire hit the soothsayers and the fortune-tellers, and they started to run away. And then the people said, "Wait, wait, you can't run away! We are using this fire to decide between the truth and the falsehood. You can't just run away like that, come back!"

So they came back again. And they said, "Okay, we're going to try it again, and this time you can't run." They said okay, they opened the door again, the fire came out, again it went to the soothsayers and the fortune-tellers,

and it hit them with such severity that they were burned alive. They were burned alive, and the two scholars of the Jews, they were untouched. When the people witnessed this, all of them accepted Judaism.
And that is how Judaism entered into [[Yemen|اليمن]]. So this is some of the background history of how Judaism came into the Arabian Peninsula and how it came into [[Yemen|اليمن]] in particular.
And going back to the dream that [[Rabiah ibn Nasr|ربيعة بن نصر]] had, that eventually the [[Abhash|أحباش]], the Habashis, they will come and they will rule [[Yemen|اليمن]].
If you look at the year of the birth of the Prophet ﷺ, the year that the Prophet ﷺ was born, it is known as [['Am al-Fil|عام الفيل]], the Year of the Elephant.

And it is known as the Year of the Elephant because that is the year that [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] came from [[Yemen|اليمن]] to destroy the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]]. He was the ruler of [[Yemen|اليمن]]. [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] was the ruler of [[Yemen|اليمن]], and he came to destroy the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]].

[[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] was the ruler of [[Yemen|اليمن]], but where was he from? [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] was a Habashi. [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] was an Ethiopian, but he became the ruler of [[Yemen|اليمن]] over time.

And this happened, this incident where [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] came from [[Yemen|اليمن]] to destroy the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]], it happened in the year that the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was born. And [[insha'Allah|إن شاء الله]], we will continue to talk about that in our next lesson [[bi-idhnillah|بإذن الله]].

review.q: Who was the individual responsible for bringing idol worship to the Arabian Peninsula?
review.a: [[Amr ibn Luhayy|عمرو بن لحي]] is identified as the person who reintroduced idolatry to the region.

review.q: What were the honorary titles used for the rulers of ancient Yemen and Ethiopia?
review.a: The ruler of [[Yemen|اليمن]] was known as the [[Tubba|تبع]], while the title for the ruler of Ethiopia was [[Najashi|نجاشي]].

review.q: Why did [[Tibban As'ad|تبان أسعد]] decide to spare the people of [[Yathrib|يثرب]] during his siege?
review.a: He was impressed by their unique character and hospitality, as they fought his army during the day but sent them food at night.

review.q: What information did Jewish scholars provide to [[Tibban As'ad|تبان أسعد]] regarding the future of [[Yathrib|يثرب]]?
review.a: They explained that the city was divinely protected because it was the destined place of migration for a future Prophet as mentioned in the [[Tawrah|توراة]].

review.q: Why did the tribe of [[Hudhayl|هذيل]] encourage the Yemeni King to attack the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]]?
review.a: They attempted to trick him into violating the sanctuary so that he would be destroyed by divine wrath.

review.q: Who was the first person in history to cover the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] with a [[kiswah|كسوة]]?
review.a: [[Tibban As'ad|تبان أسعد]] was the first to provide the cover using luxurious Yemeni cloth after seeing himself do so in a dream.

review.q: How was the truth of Judaism established over idolatry upon the King's return to [[Yemen|اليمن]]?
review.a: A 'trial by fire' occurred where a sacred fire consumed the idolatrous soothsayers but left the Jewish scholars unharmed.

review.q: What lesson does the speaker draw from the behavior of the people of [[Yathrib|يثرب]] toward their enemies?
review.a: The speaker notes that generosity and high character can serve as a powerful form of [[dawah|دَعْوَة]].
